articles.title: Fitch Ratings announces changes to Sri Lanka’s national rating scale
articles.text:
Fitch Ratings has announced the recalibration of Sri Lanka’s National Rating Scale to reflect changes in the relative creditworthiness of issuers operating in the country.
In a statement, Fitch said the recalibration follows its decision on September 22, 2026, to upgrade Sri Lanka’s sovereign Long-Term Local-Currency Issuer Default Rating (IDR) from ‘CCC+’ to ‘B-’ with a Stable Outlook.
According to Fitch, the recalibration could result in rating revisions for some issuers currently holding Sri Lankan national ratings.
The international credit rating agency stated that any such rating revisions will be announced shortly.
Fitch explained that national scale ratings are designed to rank issuers according to their relative credit risk within a particular market, helping local investors distinguish between different levels of risk.
Sri Lanka’s national ratings carry the identifier ‘(lka)’, which distinguishes them from ratings assigned under Fitch’s international rating scales.
The agency further clarified that national scale ratings cannot be directly compared with its international ratings or the national rating scales of other countries.
articles.summary: Fitch Ratings has announced the recalibration of Sri Lanka’s National Rating Scale to reflect changes in the relative creditworthiness of issuers operating in the country. The agency further clarified that national scale ratings cannot be directly compared with its international ratings or the national rating scales of other countries.

articles.title: Janith Liyanage turns self-criticism into match-winning statement against England
articles.text:
“I made a big mistake by getting out at that stage. I think, overall, we batted poorly.”
Janith Liyanage’s words after Sri Lanka’s 37-run defeat to Pakistan on October 18 were an admission of personal responsibility and a frank assessment of the team’s batting. Four days later, the Sri Lankan batter delivered a response that could hardly have been more emphatic, smashing an unbeaten 61 off 27 balls before hitting the winning six to seal a historic victory over England in Rawalpindi.
With England having piled up 429 for four, Sri Lanka needed 430 to win. After the early loss of two wickets, Avishka Fernando and Pavan Rathnayake rebuilt the innings, with Rathnayake scoring a magnificent 130 and Fernando falling just three runs short of a century. Dasun Shanaka then injected further momentum with a blistering 97 off 50 balls.
But it was Liyanage who delivered the decisive finish.
Coming in during the closing stages of the chase, he struck seven fours and three sixes at a strike rate of 225.93, keeping Sri Lanka in the hunt as the pressure mounted. With eight runs required from the final over, England briefly threatened to snatch victory as Josh Tongue claimed two wickets in consecutive deliveries. Liyanage, however, held his nerve and launched the fifth ball for six to complete Sri Lanka’s remarkable two-wicket win with one ball to spare.
His innings was not the biggest of the chase, nor was he named Player of the Match — that honour went to Rathnayake for his outstanding century. Yet Liyanage’s contribution stood out for its timing and impact, arriving when the match was on the line and finishing it with a shot that will be remembered as one of the defining moments of the game.
Sri Lanka’s victory was a collective effort, built on Pavan Rathnayake’s century, Avishka Fernando’s 97 and Dasun Shanaka’s explosive knock. But for Liyanage, the performance carried an additional significance: after publicly acknowledging his mistake in the previous match, he stepped up when his team needed him most.
If there was one player whose response to adversity deserved special recognition, Liyanage made a compelling case for that distinction in Rawalpindi.
articles.summary: “I made a big mistake by getting out at that stage. Janith Liyanage’s words after Sri Lanka’s 37-run defeat to Pakistan on October 18 were an admission of personal responsibility and a frank assessment of the team’s batting.

articles.title: Senior Professor Gallelle Sumanasiri Thera appointed Chancellor of Sabaragamuwa University
articles.text:
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed Aggamaha Panditha Senior Professor Ven. Gallelle Sumanasiri Thera as the new Chancellor of Sabaragamuwa University of Sri Lanka.
The appointment letter was presented to the Thera by Secretary to the President Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake at the Presidential Secretariat on October 23, according to the President’s Media Division (PMD).
Ven. Sumanasiri Thera, Chief Incumbent of the Kotamudungala Rajamaha Viharaya in Molagoda, previously served as Vice Chancellor of Rajarata University of Sri Lanka and the Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka.
The Thera holds a bachelor’s degree in Buddhist Philosophy and a Master of Philosophy degree from the University of Kelaniya, as well as a Master of Philosophy and a PhD from the University of Delhi, India.
He has also completed an advanced diploma in Chinese language at Peking University in China.

articles.title: Mahinda writes emotional letter to son Namal in remand custody
articles.text:
Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa has written an emotional letter to his son, MP Namal Rajapaksa, who is currently in remand custody, recalling the advice he gave him when he first entered politics in 2010.
In the letter, Mahinda Rajapaksa said Namal had sought his permission to enter politics and that he had warned him to be prepared for imprisonment and hardship.
“If you want to enter politics, do so. But be prepared to go to prison and face hardships,” the former President recalled telling his son.
He said the advice was based on his own experience of being imprisoned over what he described as baseless allegations shortly after entering politics, before Namal was born.
Mahinda Rajapaksa urged his son to maintain his faith in the judiciary, saying it had been his only source of confidence during his own imprisonment.
“Whatever anyone says, place your trust only in the judiciary,” he said.
The former President also revealed that he and his wife, Shiranthi Rajapaksa, are currently receiving treatment at Nawaloka Hospital, where Namal was born.
He said Namal’s younger brothers, Yoshitha and Rohitha, were looking after them during their hospitalisation.
Referring to legal proceedings involving Yoshitha, Mahinda Rajapaksa claimed that one case against him stemmed from his decision to join the Navy.
He also urged Namal not to seek revenge against political opponents if he returned to power, saying the children of political figures should not be held responsible for their parents’ actions.
“Children are not responsible for what their parents do. Not taking revenge is the way and tradition of the Rajapaksas,” he said.
The former President further claimed that the Rajapaksa family had been unfairly blamed despite its contribution to ending the country’s war.
Although the family had suffered electoral defeats, he urged Namal to continue believing that Sri Lankans were a grateful people.
The letter concluded with a Buddhist blessing for his son.
The letter comes as Namal Rajapaksa remains in remand custody in connection with ongoing bribery investigations. The Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court further remanded him and former Krrish Group director Janaki Siriwardena until November 6 after rejecting their bail applications in the Krrish transaction case.
articles.summary: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa has written an emotional letter to his son, MP Namal Rajapaksa, who is currently in remand custody, recalling the advice he gave him when he first entered politics in 2010. In the letter, Mahinda Rajapaksa said Namal had sought his permission to enter politics and that he had warned him to be prepared for imprisonment and hardship.

articles.title: High population density contributing to TB spread in Colombo: Health Minister
articles.text:
Minister of Health Nalinda Jayatissa says the high population density in Colombo has been a major contributing factor to the spread of tuberculosis (TB) in the city over the years.
Responding to an oral question raised by MP Mujibur Rahuman in Parliament today (23), the Minister revealed that 968 tuberculosis cases were reported in Colombo city in 2025, marking a decline compared to previous years.
According to the figures presented by the Minister, Colombo city recorded 871 tuberculosis cases in 2019, which declined to 736 in 2020 before increasing to 796 in 2021.
The number of reported cases subsequently increased to 1,093 in 2022 and 1,130 in 2023, the highest during the 2019–2025 period, before declining to 1,064 in 2024 and 968 in 2025.
Meanwhile, the Minister revealed that the Colombo District recorded 2,264 tuberculosis cases in 2015, followed by 2,156 in 2016, 2,051 in 2017 and 2,088 in 2018.
He further stated that 25% of tuberculosis cases reported in the Colombo District are from within the Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) limits.
Minister Jayatissa also pointed out that some individuals infected with tuberculosis fail to seek proper medical treatment, contributing to the continued spread of the disease.
However, he stated that free medication and appropriate treatment are being provided to patients, while mobile treatment services and X-ray examinations are also being conducted as part of efforts to control the spread of tuberculosis.
The Minister noted that tuberculosis cases reported in Colombo city have shown a declining trend since 2023, with a further reduction recorded in 2025.
articles.summary: Minister of Health Nalinda Jayatissa says the high population density in Colombo has been a major contributing factor to the spread of tuberculosis (TB) in the city over the years. Responding to an oral question raised by MP Mujibur Rahuman in Parliament today (23), the Minister revealed that 968 tuberculosis cases were reported in Colombo city in 2025, marking a decline compared to previous years.

articles.title: LankaQR users eligible for Rs. 51 Mn Lucky Draw starting October 27
articles.text:
The national QR payment adoption programme will launch its ‘Lucky Draw’ on October 27, offering a total of Rs. 51 million in cash prizes to more than 6,000 winners over six months.
According to a statement issued by GovTech Sri Lanka (Pvt.) Ltd., the nationwide programme aims to encourage the use of LankaQR payments among customers and merchants, with cash prizes of up to Rs. 1 million per winner.
All LankaQR transactions made between September 1, 2026, and February 28, 2027, will be eligible for the draw, with no separate registration required.
Under the programme, 250 winners will be selected each week to receive Rs. 5,000 each, comprising 125 customers and 125 merchants.
Meanwhile, the monthly grand draw will select six winners, including three customers and three merchants, with two winners each receiving Rs. 1 million, Rs. 500,000 and Rs. 250,000.
Each eligible LankaQR transaction, including person-to-merchant and person-to-person payments, will automatically enter both parties into the weekly and monthly draws.
GovTech stated that the first draw, scheduled for October 27, will include four weekly draws and one monthly grand draw covering transactions made in September.
Thereafter, weekly and monthly draws for each month will be conducted during the following month.
All cash prizes will be credited directly to the winners’ bank accounts.
The draws will be conducted by LankaPay, with support from GovTech, using transaction data provided by participating banks.
A designated Draw Committee, comprising representatives from the Ministry of Digital Economy, Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, Central Bank of Sri Lanka and Auditor General’s Department, will oversee the process.
According to GovTech, winners will be announced through their respective banks within two weeks of each draw, while details of prize distribution will be communicated through the Ministry of Digital Economy and GovTech.
articles.summary: The national QR payment adoption programme will launch its ‘Lucky Draw’ on October 27, offering a total of Rs. 51 million in cash prizes to more than 6,000 winners over six months. Meanwhile, the monthly grand draw will select six winners, including three customers and three merchants, with two winners each receiving Rs. 1 million, Rs. 500,000 and Rs. 250,000.

articles.title: France confirms first human infection of Shamonda livestock virus
articles.text:
French health officials on Thursday confirmed that they had detected the Shamonda virus in a human — who died early this month — in what they say was the first-ever case of a human contracting the livestock disease.
“Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans,” said France’s Ministries of Health and of Agriculture in a joint statement.
“No health risk to the general public identified at this time,” they said, adding that the human infection appeared to be, “an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient.”
The World Health Organization (WHO) said the virus was unlikely to spread.
“Based on current information and knowledge of ‌the transmission of closely related ‌viruses, ​this is an isolated human case and it is unlikely to ​lead to wider spread at this time,” WHO told ⁠Reuters ​in a ​statement.
How is Shamonda virus transmitted?
First ​identified in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, the insect-borne Shamonda virus is a variant of the Orthobunyavirus, a genus that contains 138 species, and primarily affects livestock, ‌particularly cattle.
It is transmitted by culicoides, or biting midges.
The virus has been detected in ​animals in Africa and Japan for years and has been spreading across Europe this year.
Until now, it was not thought to be transmissible to humans.
According to a press statement on the Ministry of Agriculture’s webpage , “At this stage of the investigation, the hypothesis is that the case resulted from vector-borne transmission via the bite of a culicoid midge in eastern France, a region where the virus was reported to be circulating among animals in the spring and summer of 2026.”
The ministry said biological, clinical and epidemiological investigations are being carried out by experts in human, animal and environmental health, adding that authorities at the WHO and European Center for Disease Control had been notified of the incident. (DW)
articles.summary: French health officials on Thursday confirmed that they had detected the Shamonda virus in a human — who died early this month — in what they say was the first-ever case of a human contracting the livestock disease.

articles.title: NPP Pradeshiya Sabha Chairman granted bail over alleged detention of mother and son
articles.text:
The Matara Magistrate’s Court has ordered the release on bail of the Chairman of the National People’s Power (NPP)-controlled Kirinda Puhulwella Pradeshiya Sabha and four others arrested over allegations of illegally detaining and subjecting a retired female teacher and her son to physical and mental harassment.
The five suspects, including Pradeshiya Sabha officials, were arrested by Thihagoda Police yesterday (22), following a complaint lodged by the retired teacher and her son, who is an engineer.
According to reports, the incident stemmed from a dispute over the construction of a wall along Wadigawatta Road in Kirinda.
The dispute reportedly arose after a technical officer attached to the Pradeshiya Sabha, who resides on a neighbouring property, constructed a section of a wall that obstructed the engineer from taking his vehicle out of his residence.
Following the dispute, the Pradeshiya Sabha Chairman had allegedly summoned the retired teacher and her son to the council premises to discuss the legality of the construction and prepare a report for the Human Rights Commission.
However, the two were allegedly confined to a room at the Pradeshiya Sabha premises and subjected to physical and mental harassment.
Following a complaint lodged with Thihagoda Police, investigations were launched, resulting in the arrest of five suspects over allegations including the misuse of legal and political authority.
The suspects were subsequently produced before the Matara Magistrate’s Court, where the Magistrate, after considering submissions from both parties, ordered their release on personal bail.
articles.summary: The Matara Magistrate’s Court has ordered the release on bail of the Chairman of the National People’s Power (NPP)-controlled Kirinda Puhulwella Pradeshiya Sabha and four others arrested over allegations of illegally detaining and subjecting a retired female teacher and her son to physical and mental harassment.

articles.title: New guidelines introduced to manage water and electricity use in state hospitals
articles.text:
The Ministry of Health has introduced a new set of guidelines aimed at ensuring the efficient use of water and electricity in public healthcare institutions while minimising wastage without affecting patient care.
According to a statement issued by the Ministry, the guidelines focus on monitoring water and electricity consumption, improving data reporting, ensuring proper maintenance of systems and encouraging staff participation in efficient resource management.
The Ministry stated that the guidelines were developed considering the operational requirements of healthcare institutions, particularly the need to maintain uninterrupted services in operating theatres, intensive care units, laboratories and sanitation facilities.
The initiative is expected to reduce unnecessary water and electricity consumption, improve the efficient use of public funds and strengthen the sustainability of healthcare services.
The guidelines were officially launched on Wednesday (21) at the National Hospital in Colombo, under the patronage of Deputy Minister of Health Hansaka Wijemuni, to mark World Energy Day on October 22.
The guidelines were subsequently presented to Minister of Health Nalinda Jayatissa yesterday (22) by Consultant Dr. Upuli Wijemanna, Director of the Organisational Development Unit of the Ministry’s Planning Division.
The Ministry added that the initiative aims to strengthen resource management across public healthcare institutions while ensuring the continuous delivery of quality healthcare services to the public.

articles.title: Parliamentary Committee approves Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Bill
articles.text:
The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection has approved the Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Bill, subject to amendments to certain provisions.
The Bill was discussed at a committee meeting held in Parliament on Tuesday (20), chaired by MP Najith Indika.
The proposed legislation aims to eradicate rabies in Sri Lanka through dog vaccination, population control and the regulation of commercial dog breeding.
It also seeks to formalise dog registration, establish national and regional advisory committees for rabies eradication, and replace the existing Rabies Ordinance and Dog Registration Ordinance with a new legal framework.
During discussions, the committee highlighted the need to clarify the age at which dogs should receive their first rabies vaccination.
Particular attention was also given to individuals who voluntarily feed, care for or provide medical assistance to stray dogs.
The committee discussed amendments to ensure that such individuals are not automatically considered legal owners or held responsible for all obligations applicable to dog owners simply because they assist stray animals.
Meanwhile, the committee emphasised that dog sterilisation should be carried out through surgical procedures under veterinary supervision, while concerns were raised over alternative methods, including hormonal injections.
Proposals were also discussed to revise fines for failing to register dogs, strengthen regulations governing commercial dog breeding centres and introduce stricter measures to prevent animal cruelty.
The committee further highlighted the importance of following proper veterinary procedures when handling dogs suspected of having rabies.
Discussions also focused on the establishment of national and regional advisory committees, including their responsibilities and coordination with relevant institutions.
articles.summary: The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection has approved the Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Bill, subject to amendments to certain provisions. It also seeks to formalise dog registration, establish national and regional advisory committees for rabies eradication, and replace the existing Rabies Ordinance and Dog Registration Ordinance with a new legal framework.

articles.title: Sri Lanka seeks return of six more artefacts from Netherlands
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has requested the return of six more historical artefacts from the Netherlands under the second phase of the cultural restitution process, as the two countries mark 75 years of diplomatic relations.
The request was highlighted by Deputy Minister Anil Jayantha Fernando while addressing the National Day Reception of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, held in Colombo yesterday (22).
Sri Lanka previously received six historical artefacts from the Rijksmuseum in the Netherlands in December 2023, following collaborative research into their origins.
The returned artefacts included a golden kasthana, a silver kasthana, a golden knife, two Mahathuwakku (wall guns) and Lewke Disave’s cannon.
Originating from the Kandyan Kingdom and acquired during the colonial period, the artefacts hold significant historical and cultural value for Sri Lanka.
Deputy Minister Fernando noted that their return reflected a shared commitment to mutual respect, reconciliation and the preservation of cultural heritage.
Meanwhile, highlighting tourism ties between the two countries, he said Sri Lanka welcomed 2,362,521 international tourists in 2025, marking a 15.1% increase compared to the previous year.
The Netherlands ranked ninth among Sri Lanka’s tourism source markets, with 64,164 Dutch tourists visiting the country during the year.
Deputy Minister Fernando also highlighted the longstanding relationship between Sri Lanka and the Netherlands, noting that although ties date back more than four centuries, formal diplomatic relations were established in 1951.
Over the past 75 years, bilateral cooperation has expanded across trade, investment, development, education, tourism, culture and maritime affairs.
He further identified sustainable maritime development, ocean governance, maritime security, port development and the blue economy as key areas for future cooperation.
The Netherlands has also supported Sri Lanka in agriculture, fisheries, rural development, water supply, healthcare, disaster management and food security.
Deputy Minister Fernando noted that Sri Lanka’s recognition as a country of strategic focus under the Netherlands’ International Cultural Policy for 2025–2028 would further strengthen cultural cooperation.
He also referred to the Second Round of Political Consultations held in The Hague in October 2025 and discussions between the Foreign Ministers of the two countries as important steps towards expanding bilateral relations.
Anil Jayantha Fernando reaffirmed Sri Lanka’s commitment to strengthening its partnership with the Netherlands and exploring new opportunities for cooperation as the two countries commemorate 75 years of diplomatic relations.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka has requested the return of six more historical artefacts from the Netherlands under the second phase of the cultural restitution process, as the two countries mark 75 years of diplomatic relations. Sri Lanka previously received six historical artefacts from the Rijksmuseum in the Netherlands in December 2023, following collaborative research into their origins.

articles.title: Phosphate bribery case: MP Chamara Sampath further remanded
articles.text:
Badulla District MP and former Minister Chamara Sampath Dassanayake has been further remanded until November 06 in connection with an investigation into the alleged solicitation and acceptance of Rs. 8.4 million in bribes from three phosphate-importing companies.
The order was issued by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today (23), following submissions made by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC).
The MP’s former private secretary, who was also arrested in connection with the incident, has been further remanded until the same date.
The Bribery Commission informed the court that Chamara Sampath Dassanayake is accused of accepting bribes to issue phosphate import licences to three companies without following the proper procedures during his tenure as State Minister of Primary Industries from September 08, 2022, to September 23, 2024.
The Commission further informed the court that the MP has been named as the third suspect in the case.
As investigations into the allegations are ongoing, the Bribery Commission requested that the suspects be further remanded.

articles.title: Police reject claims of questioning over ‘Was Kavi’, launch investigation
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Police have denied claims that a youth was questioned by Dematagoda Police over traditional Sinhala curse verses (was kavi), announcing that an investigation has been launched into the allegations circulating on social media.
According to a statement issued by the Police Media Division, a report was obtained from the Dematagoda Police Station following the circulation of a video claiming that Police had recorded a statement from an individual in connection with traditional Sinhala curse verses on or around October 22.
However, Dematagoda Police have confirmed that no complaint regarding such verses had been received and that no statements had been recorded from any individual in connection with the matter.
The Police Media Division further stated that claims made on social media by Attorney-at-Law Sudath Kumararatne regarding the alleged questioning were false.
Accordingly, the Central Crime Investigation Bureau has commenced an investigation into the claims on the instructions of the Inspector General of Police (IGP).
Previously, Kumararatne, a lawyer affiliated with the opposition Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), had claimed that Dematagoda Police summoned and questioned one of his clients over traditional Sinhala curse verses that circulated widely on social media during a recent protest by Buddhist monks.
He alleged that his client had been questioned about whether he had written the verses, which reportedly began with an invocation to the deity Vajrapani.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Police have denied claims that a youth was questioned by Dematagoda Police over traditional Sinhala curse verses (was kavi), announcing that an investigation has been launched into the allegations circulating on social media. The Police Media Division further stated that claims made on social media by Attorney-at-Law Sudath Kumararatne regarding the alleged questioning were false.

articles.title: “Be part of Sri Lanka’s growth”: Chathuranga invites global investors at NDTV summit
articles.text:
Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe has invited global investors to become partners in Sri Lanka’s next phase of economic growth, urging them to move beyond supporting the country’s economic recovery.
“Don’t just support Sri Lanka’s recovery, be part of its growth,” the Deputy Minister said while participating in a discussion titled “Sri Lanka’s Economic Reset: Recovery, Resilience and the Road Ahead” at the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi, India.
According to a statement issued by the Deputy Minister’s Office, Abeysinghe highlighted Sri Lanka’s potential to become a regional hub for trade, industry, technology, research and development, and skilled talent as the country transitions from economic stabilisation towards sustainable growth.
He outlined plans to establish 18 new industrial zones, including 11 through the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development and seven through the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI), to expand industrial capacity and create new opportunities for local and international businesses.
The Deputy Minister also encouraged foreign companies to establish partnerships with Sri Lankan enterprises through investment, technology transfer and greater access to international markets.
Highlighting opportunities for stronger economic cooperation between Sri Lanka and India, he identified manufacturing, agricultural value addition, logistics, renewable energy, marine industries and technology as key sectors for potential partnerships.
Abeysinghe further pointed to ongoing efforts to simplify investment procedures, digitise public services and strengthen regulatory clarity to create a more investor-friendly business environment.

articles.title: WMO forecasts stronger El Niño conditions from November 2026 to January 2027
articles.text:
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has forecast a further intensification of El Niño conditions between November 2026 and January 2027, with warming expected to peak around December 2026.
According to the WMO’s Global Seasonal Climate Update for November 2026 to January 2027, multi-model forecasts indicate a strengthening of El Niño conditions in the Pacific Ocean over the coming months.
The seasonal average sea surface temperature anomaly in the Niño 3.4 region is projected to reach approximately 3.8°C above normal during the three-month period, with warming expected to peak in December.
The WMO stated that the relatively narrow differences among individual forecast models indicate a high level of confidence in the projections.
Meanwhile, in the Indian Ocean, the positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is expected to weaken towards normal conditions, with a seasonal average anomaly of approximately +0.3°C.
Sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Atlantic Ocean are also forecast to remain warmer than normal, with above-average temperatures expected in both the North and South Tropical Atlantic regions.
The WMO’s Global Seasonal Climate Update is issued monthly and provides forecasts of global temperature and rainfall patterns for the coming three months, helping countries prepare for potential climate-related impacts. (Newswire)

articles.title: Sri Lanka records decline in shootings in 2026: Public Security Minister
articles.text:
Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala says shooting incidents linked to organized crime have declined to 18 so far in 2026, compared to 29 incidents recorded in 2025.
Addressing Parliament today (23), the Minister said the authorities have managed to bring the situation under control to some extent through intensified operations targeting organized criminal gangs and drug trafficking networks.
Providing statistics on murders and shootings linked to organized crime, Wijepala said two incidents were recorded in 2020, four in 2021, 23 in 2022, 16 in 2023, 42 in 2024, 29 in 2025 and 18 so far in 2026.
He said a total of 134 such incidents had been recorded during the period from 2020 to 2026.
The Minister attributed the increase in shooting incidents in previous years to conflicts between organized criminal gangs and drug trafficking networks.
He further revealed that INTERPOL red notices have been issued for 236 Sri Lankans, including 94 individuals identified as organized criminals and drug traffickers.
Of those wanted, 30 are sought in connection with murders, while others are wanted for drug trafficking and other serious crimes.
Wijepala said 17 special teams have been deployed to carry out operations aimed at curbing organized crime and drug trafficking across the country.
He added that measures are being taken to suppress criminal activities locally while also working to bring back drug traffickers operating from overseas.
The Minister reiterated that these efforts have helped contain the situation to some extent, with shooting incidents declining this year.

articles.title: Two killed, 15 injured in bus accident in Saliyawewa
articles.text:
Two people were killed and 15 others injured in an accident involving a luxury passenger bus and a motorcycle in the Saliyawewa Police Division yesterday (22).
According to Police, the accident occurred near the Mahahenyaya Junction on the Puttalam–Trincomalee Road when a luxury passenger bus travelling from Colombo to Mannar collided with a motorcycle travelling ahead in the same direction.
Following the collision, the bus driver lost control of the vehicle, causing it to crash into a nearby bridge before hitting a high-voltage electricity pole and overturning.
The motorcycle rider, bus driver, conductor and 14 bus passengers sustained injuries and were admitted to the Puttalam Hospital.
However, the motorcycle rider and a female passenger travelling in the bus succumbed to their injuries after being admitted to the hospital.
The deceased have been identified as a 38-year-old resident of Saliyawewa and a 30-year-old woman from Rambewa.
Saliyawewa Police are conducting further investigations into the accident. (Newswire/ Image- Accident1st)

articles.title: Namal questions whether IGP will face same law as Gnanasara Thera
articles.text:

Addressing Parliament, Rajapaksa questioned what action would be taken against the IGP over allegations that he had disregarded a court order and provided false information to court in connection with cases filed against innocent individuals.

He pointed out that the Government had repeatedly pledged to ensure equal application of the law, irrespective of an individual’s position or status.
“The President has said that the law is equal for everyone. We are waiting to see what happens to the IGP,” he said.
Meanwhile, Rajapaksa criticised the Government’s approach to combating narcotics, claiming that its focus on arrests and remanding suspects had failed to address the root causes of drug trafficking.
He argued that setting daily arrest targets for police officers was ineffective, adding that authorities should instead focus on individuals responsible for importing and distributing narcotics while providing rehabilitation for drug-dependent individuals.
The MP also raised concerns over prison overcrowding, claiming that the increasing number of arrests had placed additional pressure on the prison system.
He further questioned the effectiveness of ongoing anti-drug operations, pointing out that narcotics remained available and shooting incidents continued despite reports of major drug and firearm seizures.
Rajapaksa also highlighted the shortage of prison officers and called for improved working conditions, risk allowances and greater support for the families of officers who had died in the line of duty.

articles.title: Seven killed in six accidents across Sri Lanka in one day
articles.text:
Seven people, including an Air Force serviceman and two women, were killed in six separate accidents reported across Sri Lanka on October 22, according to police.
The accidents occurred in Habaraduwa, Chunnakam, Mahawa, Pussellawa and Kelaniya, with two deaths reported in the Pussellawa accident.
In Habaraduwa, a 40-year-old Air Force serviceman from Medagama was killed after being struck by a train travelling from Beliatta to Maradana. Police said the serviceman had been returning to report for duty after taking leave.
In Chunnakam, a 67-year-old cyclist died after being struck by a tipper truck near the Inuvil Kandasamy Kovil Junction on the Jaffna-Kankesanthurai Road. The cyclist died after being admitted to Jaffna Hospital. The truck driver was arrested.
In Mahawa, a 78-year-old pedestrian from Galgamuwa was killed after being struck by a bus near the weekly fair junction on the Madagalla-Daladagama Road. The bus driver was arrested.
In Pussellawa, two people were killed when a cab veered off the road and overturned down a slope while travelling from Kadadora Junction towards Kotagepitiya. The 57-year-old driver died at the scene, while a 55-year-old woman travelling in the vehicle died after being admitted to Gampola Hospital.
Meanwhile, in Kelaniya, a 34-year-old woman from Kandana died after a car veered off the Biyagama-Colombo Road in Pilapitiya, struck her and subsequently crashed into an electricity pole. The woman died while receiving treatment at the National Hospital in Colombo. The driver was arrested.
Police said investigations into all the incidents are continuing.

articles.title: “If England can do it, why can’t we?” – Dasun Shanaka reveals mindset behind historic chase
articles.text:
Sri Lankan all-rounder Dasun Shanaka has revealed how a positive dressing-room mindset, tactical decisions and confidence inspired by England’s batting performance helped Sri Lanka pull off a historic 430-run chase in Rawalpindi.
Sri Lanka secured a thrilling two-wicket victory over England, completing the second-highest successful run chase in men’s ODI history with one ball remaining.
Speaking during a post-match interview, Shanaka, who smashed 97 off 50 balls, said the team had entered the chase with a clear plan despite England posting a mammoth 429.
Shanaka credited the team leadership for preparing the players mentally and establishing a clear approach to the game.
He said Harry Brook’s extraordinary double century had also inspired the Sri Lankan players to believe they could produce a similarly exceptional batting performance.
“If they can do that, why can’t our team do that?” Shanaka said, recalling the discussion among the players.
He explained that the team knew defeat would leave them almost out of the competition, making it essential to approach the chase with an attacking mindset.
Shanaka also revealed that Janith Liyanage had discussed the possibility of promoting him up the batting order with the coach Gary Kirsten, while the captain was also involved in the decision.
“I think it was the right decision to make in this game,” Shanaka said, describing the move as a turning point.
The former Sri Lanka captain praised Pavan Rathnayake and Avishka Fernando for laying the foundation for the chase after Sri Lanka lost two early wickets, including the run-out of their captain.
Rathnayake struck a magnificent 130, while Fernando contributed 97 in his return to the team.
Shanaka said their partnership gave him the belief that Sri Lanka could successfully chase down the target.
“The way Pavan and Avishka batted, that’s where I felt that the game is on,” he said.
He explained that his initial focus was on timing the ball, building momentum and taking the chase deep rather than attempting to finish the match too early.
Shanaka also praised Liyanage for holding his nerve during the final stages and hitting the winning six.
He said the victory was particularly significant for Sri Lankan cricket, demonstrating the team’s potential despite several match-winning players being unavailable.
Shanaka described the result as a major confidence boost for both the players and Sri Lankan cricket supporters.
“I feel it’s a very good booster to Sri Lankan cricket and for the players and to everyone that we can do this. So keep believing,” he said.
The historic victory came after Sri Lanka had suffered a defeat against Pakistan earlier in the tournament, making the comeback even more significant.
Sri Lanka’s successful chase of 430 ranks second only to South Africa’s famous 438-run chase against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 in men’s ODI history.

articles.title: What did Sanga & Nasser Hussain say about Sri Lanka’s historic win
articles.text:
Former Sri Lanka captain Kumar Sangakkara and former England captain Nasser Hussain have praised Sri Lanka’s extraordinary record-breaking ODI run chase against England in Rawalpindi, describing it as a special moment for Sri Lankan cricket while stressing that significant improvements are still needed.
Sri Lanka chased down England’s massive total of 429, reaching 430/8 with one ball remaining to complete the second-highest successful run chase in men’s ODI history.
Speaking during a post-match television discussion, both former captains highlighted Sri Lanka’s batting approach, improved decision-making and the match-winning contributions of Pavan Rathnayake, Avishka Fernando, Dasun Shanaka and Janith Liyanage.
Hussain described the victory as an exceptional achievement and said Sri Lanka needed a moment of this magnitude.
“Sri Lanka are such a talented, passionate cricketing nation. They needed a day like today. They got a day like today,” Hussain said.
However, Sangakkara cautioned against allowing the historic victory to overshadow areas requiring attention.
“Enjoy the result tonight and then start talking about bowling, our fielding, the calmness in that first 10 overs that we require,” Sangakkara said.
He stressed that the coaching staff, selectors and players must remain focused on improving consistency and decision-making ahead of the World Cup.
Sangakkara calls for consistency in selection
Sangakkara praised Sri Lanka’s decision to promote Dasun Shanaka up the batting order, saying tactical flexibility and identifying the right players for particular situations were essential in modern white-ball cricket.
Shanaka smashed 97 off 50 balls, playing a crucial role in keeping Sri Lanka’s record chase alive.
Sangakkara said the decision reflected better game awareness from the team management, adding that the timing of batting changes could significantly influence the outcome of matches.
He also called for consistency in player selection, particularly in the case of Pavan Rathnayake, who scored a match-winning 130.
Hussain echoed those sentiments, describing Rathnayake as a player with exceptional talent who should be backed over a longer period.
“You’ve got to stick with him now. You’ve got to stick with him for a long time,” Hussain said.
Sangakkara said players should ultimately be assessed on their performances rather than excessive scrutiny of their batting techniques.
He also noted that Avishka Fernando had strengthened his case for a consistent place in the team following his impressive return.
Hussain praises Liyanage’s composure
Hussain reserved special praise for Janith Liyanage, who held his nerve during the final stages of the chase after Sri Lanka appeared to be losing momentum.
He said the pressure of completing a historic chase could be greater than the pressure experienced earlier in the innings.
According to Hussain, Liyanage displayed the calmness and composure required to finish the game, striking the decisive six to secure victory.
Sangakkara agreed, explaining that successful players must remain focused on the present rather than worrying about failure or anticipating victory.
Historic win, but work remains
Despite praising Sri Lanka’s batting performance, Sangakkara said the team must address weaknesses in bowling, fielding and its approach during the opening overs.
He also emphasized the need for consistent communication between coaches, analysts, selectors and players.
Hussain, meanwhile, questioned England’s inability to defend 429, pointing to their struggles to take wickets during the middle overs.
Both former captains also acknowledged Harry Brook’s extraordinary double century, which helped England post their imposing total.
Sangakkara said Sri Lanka should celebrate the historic achievement but avoid treating one exceptional performance as evidence that all the team’s problems had been resolved.
The victory places Sri Lanka behind only South Africa’s famous 438-run chase against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 on the list of highest successful men’s ODI run chases.
articles.summary: Former Sri Lanka captain Kumar Sangakkara and former England captain Nasser Hussain have praised Sri Lanka’s extraordinary record-breaking ODI run chase against England in Rawalpindi, describing it as a special moment for Sri Lankan cricket while stressing that significant improvements are still needed.

articles.title: Sajith questions 2027 Budget without disclosure of 2026 Budget progress
articles.text:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa queried the government in Parliament today ( Oct.22), asking how a new budget for 2027 can be presented without first disclosing the progress and implementation status of the 2026 budget.
Raising a question under Standing Order 27(2), the Opposition Leader pointed out that since the 2027 budget is scheduled to be presented in just three weeks on November 12, the government cannot delay providing answers regarding the progress of the 2026 budget proposals.
He emphasized that merely allocating provisions for budget proposals does not fulfill expected development and economic goals, and that it is the government’s responsibility to ensure these proposals are implemented effectively to yield results matching public expenditures.
The Opposition Leader demanded disclosure of the financial and physical progress, allocated funds, utilized expenditures and remaining balances under each ministry as of September 30, 2026. He also requested details on how domestic and foreign sources were allocated for special projects across the 28 fields outlined in the Main Public Investment Projects Summary issued by the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development on November 7, 2025, along with their financial and physical progress as of September 30.
Further, the Opposition Leader called for action plans regarding programs scheduled to be completed or implemented during the remainder of 2026, the utilization of remaining provisions, expected expenditures, timelines, and the government’s approach toward unutilized funds at year-end. He asked for clarification on current progress concerning capital expenditure and microfinance given reports that state revenue rose to 75.5% of annual estimates within the first eight months according to Daily FT.
He also pressed the government for details on revisions or reallocations of provisions originally assigned to ministries in 2026, including the reasons, approval procedures, responsible officials, and the current progress and completion timelines of development projects funded by foreign aid or loans. Additionally, he requested targets for Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs) in 2026, actual FDIs attracted as of September 30, and the primary economic sectors and source countries involved.
Concluding his queries, the Opposition Leader asked for information on the number of state-owned enterprises, their profit and loss figures during the first three quarters of 2026, steps taken to improve financial performance for loss-making entities, and estimated allocations and objectives if provisions are assigned to them in the 2027 budget. Stating that the opposition will not shape its questions according to the government’s or the Leader of the House’s preferences, he asserted that the 2027 budget speech cannot proceed without answers to these progress reports.
articles.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa queried the government in Parliament today ( Oct.22), asking how a new budget for 2027 can be presented without first disclosing the progress and implementation status of the 2026 budget.

With the completion of the Galle project, model villages have now been launched and handed over in 21 other districts, including Batticaloa, Vavuniya, Jaffna, Kandy, Gampaha, Anuradhapura, Badulla, Matale, Puttalam, Colombo, Trincomalee, Monaragala, Kilinochchi, Mannar, Mullaitivu, Ratnapura, Ampara, Kurunegala, Kegalle, Kalutara and Polonnaruwa.
The overall project has achieved nearly 98.6% progress, with the final three model villages expected to be handed over to beneficiaries soon. The inauguration ceremony was also attended by District Parliamentarians, the Chairman and senior officials of the National Housing Development Authority, and representatives from the Galle district administration.

Beyond the shared values, the partnership holds a personal significance for the founder of DINIDU, a proud Royalist who views this as an opportunity to give back to his alma mater.

Beyond a contest between two rowing crews, the Royal–Thomian Regatta represents generations of sporting heritage, bringing together students, alumni and supporters through a shared appreciation for competition and the friendships formed along the way.
By supporting the 55th edition, DINIDU hopes to celebrate these traditions while recognising the determination and commitment of young athletes who dedicate themselves to their sport.

articles.title: Sri Lanka seeks to safeguard EU GSP+ access in talks with Romanian lawmakers
articles.text:
Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Employment Arun Hemachandra focused on securing Sri Lanka’s continued access to the European Union’s GSP+ trade preferences during high-level bilateral talks with Romanian parliamentarians in Bucharest.
Meeting at the Romanian Parliament, Hemachandra held discussions with Marius-Constantin Budăi, President of the Romania–Sri Lanka Parliamentary Friendship Group and former Minister of Labour; Cristina -Mădălina Prună, Member of Parliament and Vice-Chairperson of the Committee on Industries and Services; and Cristian Alexandru Popa, Member of Parliament and Secretary of the Parliamentary Friendship Group.
Highlighting the vital role GSP+ access plays in Sri Lanka’s exports, the Deputy Minister explored pathways to expand economic cooperation with Romania and the broader European market. The dialogue also touched upon strengthening parliamentary relations, expanding bilateral trade and investment, boosting tourism, and fostering educational and people to people exchanges.
Special attention was given to the welfare of Sri Lankan workers in Romania, including ethical recruitment, labour rights, social protection and skilled employment opportunities. Additionally, both sides discussed enhancing engagement with European parliamentary institutions, building on the recent 12th EU–Sri Lanka Inter-Parliamentary Meeting held in Brussels.
The Sri Lankan delegation included Samantha Pathirana, Sri Lankan Ambassador to Romania; Dilani Weerakoon, Director General of the Europe and North America Division; and Prarthana Kaushalya Govinda, Counsellor at the Sri Lankan Embassy in Bucharest.

articles.title: ADB approves $100 million to strengthen social protection and livelihoods in Sri Lanka
articles.text:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $100 million in financing, consisting of a $50 million policy based loan and a $50 million project loan to strengthen social protection, economic inclusion and resilience for the poor and elderly in Sri Lanka.
The initiative, named the Promoting Resilience and Opportunity for Inclusive Recovery Sector Development Programme, aims to help the government expand livelihood and employment opportunities for low income households, enhance eldercare services and boost the responsiveness of the country’s social protection system. ADB Country Director for Sri Lanka Shannon Cowlin noted that the programme will ensure economic recovery translates into meaningful improvements for vulnerable populations.
While Sri Lanka continues its economic recovery, poverty and vulnerability remain high, particularly among women, youth, the elderly, persons with disabilities and populations in rural or disadvantaged areas.
The programme directly addresses these challenges through policy reforms, institutional strengthening, and strategic investments.
To support livelihoods, the programme will assist the implementation of the government’s National Empowerment Programme by providing 30,000 households identified through the Aswesuma social registry across six districts with livelihood grants, employment and business support, skills development, financial literacy training and access to reliable markets.
Regarding eldercare, the programme will strengthen the policy and regulatory framework while establishing five model elderly day care centers in poorer districts to provide integrated support services and serve as demonstration sites for nationwide scaling.
Additionally, the programme will enhance social protection delivery by upgrading digital platforms, monitoring systems, case management, and data governance, alongside measures to improve shock responsiveness during climate-related emergencies and other crises.
articles.summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $100 million in financing, consisting of a $50 million policy based loan and a $50 million project loan to strengthen social protection, economic inclusion and resilience for the poor and elderly in Sri Lanka.

articles.title: CAA launches islandwide raids following reports of wheat flour price hike
articles.text:
The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has launched islandwide market inspections and raids following reports of an increase in the price of a kilogram of wheat flour.
According to the CAA, although media reports indicate that the price of wheat flour has increased, the relevant manufacturing companies have neither held prior discussions with nor informed the CAA of such a price increase.
Wheat flour has been designated as a specified commodity under Section 18 of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act, No. 9 of 2003. Accordingly, prior written approval from the Authority is required before increasing the price of such a commodity.
The relevant manufacturing companies have already been requested to provide explanations for the wheat flour price increase and details of the price revision.
Further action will be determined after considering the explanations provided by the manufacturing companies and the findings of the ongoing investigations. Legal action will be taken against traders found selling wheat flour in violation of applicable laws, as well as against manufacturers and distributors if investigations establish legal violations.

articles.title: Police question man over viral curse verses allegedly targeting government: Lawyer
articles.text:
A lawyer affiliated with the opposition Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) has claimed that Dematagoda Police summoned and questioned one of his clients over traditional Sinhala curse verses (was kavi) that circulated widely on social media during a recent protest by Buddhist monks.
Attorney-at-Law Sudath Kumararatne said his client had been questioned about whether he had written the verses, which begin with an invocation to the deity Vajrapani.
According to Kumararatne, police asked his client whether he had authored the verses, assisted anyone in preparing them or had any knowledge of their creation.
He said his client denied any involvement and told police that he did not have the ability to compose such verses.
Kumararatne questioned the legal basis for the inquiry, arguing that Sri Lankan law contained no specific legislation prohibiting curse verses, black magic or similar traditional practices.
He alleged that some within the government appeared to have become alarmed by the circulation of the verses.
The lawyer also claimed that police had no legal grounds to summon individuals for questioning solely over such verses.
Responding to questions from journalists, Kumararatne declined to identify his client, citing professional ethics and lawyer-client confidentiality.
However, he maintained that the incident had taken place and challenged journalists to verify the matter with officers at Dematagoda Police Station.
He urged the government to focus on addressing public concerns rather than investigating traditional curse verses.
“If the government is still afraid, they should get someone to recite a blessing poem,” he remarked.
The allegations come amid continuing protests by Buddhist monks demanding an unconditional presidential pardon for Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera.
Police have not independently confirmed the alleged questioning or clarified whether an investigation is underway.
articles.summary: A lawyer affiliated with the opposition Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) has claimed that Dematagoda Police summoned and questioned one of his clients over traditional Sinhala curse verses (was kavi) that circulated widely on social media during a recent protest by Buddhist monks. articles.title: Gateway College Crowned TISSL Basketball Champions
articles.text:
Gateway College has firmly cemented its status as the undisputed powerhouse of schools’ basketball, capturing The International Schools of Sri Lanka (TISSL) Under-19 Championship for a spectacular fifth consecutive year.
The historic victory underscores a legacy of excellence, discipline, and relentless determination that has come to define Gateway’s basketball program. Being unbeaten in the tournament, Gateway showcased unmatched tactical brilliance, superior fitness, and clinical execution on the court to retain their crown once again.
Gateway began its campaign with convincing victories over Wycherley International School Colombo (WISC), 59–25, and Colombo International School Kandy (CISK), 60–25. In a closely contested match, GCC edged past British School in Colombo (BSC) 46–45.
In the quarter-finals, Gateway dominated Colombo International School Colombo (CISC), winning 84–44, before defeating Elizabeth Moir School (EMS) 72–35 in the semi-finals. The team carried this momentum into the final, securing a convincing 55–39 victory over Asian International School (AIS) to claim the championship.
Captain Anujitha Samarasundara was named Most Valuable Player (MVP) for his outstanding contribution to the team’s success. Jehan Ranawaka received the Best Defensive Player (BDP) award, while Ashkenz Gunasekara of AIS was recognised as the Best Offensive Player (BOP).

articles.title: Hemas Hospitals Brings a New Global Standard of MRI Technology to Sri Lanka
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s first MRI with Siemens Healthineers’ Deep Resolve AI technology sets a new national benchmark in diagnostic imaging, bringing a level of capability not previously available in the country and marking another step forward in advancing Sri Lanka’s healthcare standards.
Hemas Hospitals has brought a new class of MRI technology to Sri Lanka with the introduction of the Siemens Healthineers MAGNETOM Sola 1.5T at Hemas Capital Hospital, Thalawathugoda. Considered a global benchmark in advanced, patient-centric MRI imaging, the system gives Sri Lankan patients access to capabilities at the forefront of modern diagnostic imaging.
The system is the first MRI in Sri Lanka to feature Siemens Healthineers’ Deep Resolve AI-based image reconstruction technology, introducing a combination of artificial intelligence, advanced image quality, speed and patient comfort not previously available in the country.
This is more than an incremental upgrade in MRI capability. It represents a significant technological leap and establishes a new national benchmark for diagnostic imaging in Sri Lanka.
For Hemas Hospitals, it is also an important milestone in a much larger journey. Continued investment in advanced medical technology, clinical capability and healthcare infrastructure is intended not only to support the organisation’s next phase of growth, but also to help raise standards of care across Sri Lanka, expand access to world-class capabilities locally and demonstrate the meaningful role that responsible private healthcare investment can play in building a healthier nation.
A different class of MRI for Sri Lanka
The sophistication of the system behind an examination can have a significant impact on the quality of imaging, the time required to complete a scan, patient comfort and the overall safety of the experience.
The MAGNETOM Sola brings to Sri Lanka an MRI platform incorporating technology at the leading edge of global imaging innovation.
Its Deep Resolve technology uses artificial intelligence during image reconstruction to generate highly detailed images in significantly shorter examination times. According to Siemens Healthineers, a brain scan reconstructed using Deep Resolve can be completed in approximately half the time of a conventional scan while achieving twice the resolution.
For Sri Lankan patients, this means access to a level of imaging capability that has until now not been available locally.
The benefits are also immediately felt during the examination itself. Shorter scan times can mean less time inside the MRI, making the experience easier for patients who may experience anxiety or claustrophobia, as well as elderly patients, children and those who find it difficult to remain still for extended periods.
A complete knee examination can be performed with approximately three minutes of scan time, while certain examinations of the bile ducts can be completed in a single breath-hold of as little as 13 seconds.
The system also supports sophisticated applications including advanced cardiac MRI, further expanding the diagnostic capabilities available at Hemas Capital Hospital.
With its introduction, Hemas Hospitals is raising the benchmark for what an MRI experience in Sri Lanka can be.
Bringing the standards of leading global healthcare closer to home
The significance of this investment extends beyond diagnostic imaging.
For Hemas Hospitals, the new MRI reflects a broader ambition to ensure that Sri Lankan patients increasingly have access to healthcare technology and capabilities comparable with those found at leading healthcare institutions internationally.
Rather than requiring patients to look beyond Sri Lanka for the latest advancements in healthcare, Hemas is investing to bring those capabilities closer to home.
The MRI at Thalawathugoda is one of the early milestones in this next phase.
Hemas Hospitals is continuing to strengthen its clinical capabilities, technology and infrastructure as it prepares for future growth, with a focus not simply on increasing capacity, but on progressively elevating the standard of healthcare available in the country.
The organisation’s approach is centred on bringing together advanced medical technology, strong clinical expertise and a better patient experience.
In doing so, Hemas aims to contribute towards a healthier nation while helping Sri Lanka move closer to the highest standards of healthcare internationally.
The beginning of a bigger chapter
The introduction of this MRI comes at an important point in the evolution of Hemas Hospitals.
As the organisation enters its next phase of growth, further investments in healthcare infrastructure, technology and clinical capability are expected to build upon the foundation being created today.
The new MRI therefore represents one of the first tangible examples of the direction in which Hemas Hospitals is evolving.
It is a journey centred on strengthening the capabilities available within Sri Lanka, creating greater access to advanced care and building healthcare environments equipped to meet the expectations of patients well into the future.
Artificial intelligence will increasingly support that journey. Within the new MRI, AI is already working across areas such as image reconstruction and examination optimisation, enabling technology to support both clinicians and patients in practical ways.
For Hemas, however, technology is ultimately valuable because of what it enables: better diagnostics, better experiences and a higher standard of healthcare.
Dr. Lakith Peiris, Managing Director of Hemas Hospitals and Diagnostics Chain, said:
“This is a significant advancement not only for Hemas Hospitals, but for MRI imaging in Sri Lanka. We are bringing into the country a level of capability that has not previously been available here and giving our patients access to technology that sits at the forefront of modern diagnostic imaging.
“Our ambition is for Sri Lankan patients to have access to healthcare technology and clinical capabilities that stand alongside those available at leading institutions internationally. They should not have to look beyond Sri Lanka to access global standards of care and best healthcare practices.
“This MRI is an important milestone, but it is also the beginning of a much larger journey for Hemas Hospitals. As we enter our next phase of growth, we will continue investing in technology, infrastructure and clinical capability to help elevate healthcare standards and contribute towards a healthier Sri Lanka.”
Dr. Pradeep Edward, Director General Manager of Hemas Capital Hospital Pvt Ltd, said:
“What makes this technology different is not simply what the machine can do, but what that means for the patient. It enables us to combine highly advanced imaging with faster examinations and a more comfortable overall experience.
“For patients undergoing an MRI at Hemas Capital Hospital, this represents access to a standard of technology that Sri Lanka has not experienced before.
“That is the direction in which we want to continue taking healthcare at Hemas, combining excellent clinical expertise with some of the most advanced technology available to deliver an exceptional standard of care.”
The arrival of the Siemens Healthineers MAGNETOM Sola marks a new chapter for MRI in Sri Lanka and the beginning of a broader period of advancement for Hemas Hospitals.
As Hemas continues to invest in its future, the objective is clear: to bring the standards, capabilities and technologies shaping healthcare globally closer to Sri Lankan patients.
The Siemens Healthineers MAGNETOM Sola 1.5T MRI is now available at Hemas Capital Hospital, Thalawathugoda.

According to police, the incident occurred at around 10 p.m. on October 20, when the woman heard cats crying behind her house and discovered that one of them had fallen into a well.
She went to the well with her father and used the flashlight on her mobile phone to locate the trapped cat.
While her father was preparing to rescue the animal using a bucket attached to a rope, she leaned over the well to provide light.
Police said she accidentally fell into the well, reportedly striking her head against a concrete section during the fall.
She was subsequently rescued with the assistance of a relative and rushed to Wathupitiwala Hospital in Nittambuwa, where she was pronounced dead.
The woman had been employed at a glove manufacturing company in Kalagedihena, Nittambuwa, and lived with her parents and younger brother.
Warakapola Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.

articles.title: Duminda Hulangamuwa was never Ranil’s economic adviser: Bimal responds to Harsha
articles.text:
Minister Bimal Rathnayake has rejected a claim made by opposition MP Harsha de Silva that Duminda Hulangamuwa, the current economic adviser to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, had previously served as an economic adviser to former President Ranil Wickremesinghe.
Responding to remarks made by de Silva in Parliament on Wednesday (21), Rathnayake said the claim was completely false and called on the opposition MP to correct his statement.
Rathnayake said Hulangamuwa had never served as an economic adviser to Wickremesinghe or any previous president or prime minister.
He explained that Hulangamuwa had served on various committees during his tenure as chairman of the Ceylon Chamber of Commerce, but those positions were connected to his role in the business community and were not appointments as Wickremesinghe’s economic adviser.
The minister further claimed that Hulangamuwa only accepted a formal economic advisory position under the National People’s Power (NPP) government.
He urged de Silva to withdraw or correct his remarks.
The response followed de Silva’s statement in Parliament questioning why the current government was relying on the same economic expert whom he claimed had advised the previous administration, despite its criticism of Wickremesinghe’s economic policies.
Hulangamuwa was formally appointed as a senior adviser on economic affairs and finance to President Dissanayake, effective September 24, 2024.
He also serves as chairman of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka.

articles.title: New fuel price fears as global oil prices skyrocket
articles.text:
Global oil prices surged to their highest levels since May on Thursday (October 22), as escalating tensions in the Middle East and renewed attacks on Saudi Arabia raised fears of further disruptions to international oil supplies.
Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, rose 3.08% to USD 112.17 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude climbed to USD 99.83 per barrel, according to Reuters.
The sharp increase followed a series of attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement on targets in Saudi Arabia, including an oil field and a civilian airport.
At least three people were killed in the attacks, further heightening concerns over the security of energy infrastructure in the region.
Meanwhile, the United States moved to withdraw some diplomatic personnel and their families from Saudi Arabia and other missions in the Middle East amid fears of further escalation.
Reports of explosions in southern Iran and continuing threats to commercial shipping around the Strait of Hormuz also added to market uncertainty.
The Strait of Hormuz is a strategically important waterway for global energy shipments, and any further disruption could place additional pressure on international oil prices.
The latest surge has renewed concerns about rising fuel costs and broader inflationary pressures in oil-importing countries, including Sri Lanka.
However, the impact on domestic fuel prices will depend on international market trends, procurement costs and local pricing decisions.

articles.title: Patali seeks probe into Rs. 450,000 spent to bring witness from Germany
articles.text:
A complaint has been filed seeking an investigation into the alleged expenditure of approximately Rs. 450,000 in public funds to bring a witness from Germany to Sri Lanka to testify in a case involving former Minister Patali Champika Ranawaka.
According to a media statement issued today (22), the complaint was submitted by Senior Attorney-at-Law Shiral Lakthilaka on behalf of Ranawaka’s legal team, raising concerns over the alleged misuse of provisions under the Assistance to and Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses Act.
The complaint is to be handed over to the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses and the Attorney General’s Department by Attorneys-at-Law Rajika Kodithuwakku and Thikshana Gammanpila.
The complaint relates to testimony given on October 19, 2026, in case No. HC 1824/20, currently being heard before the Colombo High Court.
According to the statement, the witness had previously informed court through his lawyers that he was unable to travel to Sri Lanka to testify at the original trial.
However, approximately Rs. 450,000 had reportedly been spent on air travel and related expenses to bring the witness from Germany to Sri Lanka.
During his testimony, the witness had reportedly stated that he had not personally paid for his travel expenses and had identified the person who covered the costs as “Mr. Indika, the Director of the CCD.”
The complaint calls for an investigation into whether the legally prescribed procedures for obtaining testimony from overseas witnesses were followed and whether the expenditure complied with relevant financial regulations governing public funds.
It also raises concerns over possible improper interference in matters relating to witnesses and seeks to determine whether the arrangements could have affected the witness’s independence or the fairness of the judicial proceedings.
Ranawaka’s legal team has requested an independent investigation, an audit of the alleged expenditure of public funds and appropriate legal action against any individuals found to have violated the law.
The complaint further emphasises the importance of safeguarding the rule of law, accountability in the use of public funds and the independence of judicial proceedings.
articles.summary: A complaint has been filed seeking an investigation into the alleged expenditure of approximately Rs. 450,000 in public funds to bring a witness from Germany to Sri Lanka to testify in a case involving former Minister Patali Champika Ranawaka. However, approximately Rs. 450,000 had reportedly been spent on air travel and related expenses to bring the witness from Germany to Sri Lanka.

articles.title: “Resign or pardon Gnanasara Thera” Protesting monks issue ultimatum to President
articles.text:
Ven. Balangoda Kassapa Thera, who is continuing a protest at Colombo’s Viharamahadevi Park demanding the release of Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, has called on President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to either resign or grant a presidential pardon to the imprisoned monk.
Speaking during the ongoing satyagraha despite heavy rain, Kassapa Thera also alleged that two individuals carrying weapons had been sent to the protest site on October 21.
“Yesterday, two armed individuals were sent here. They stood behind us and shouted abuse using obscene language,” the Thera claimed.
He also issued a warning to the government, referring to its political headquarters in Pelawatte.
“We tell the Pelawatte office that if they are trying to create violent confrontations to stop this protest, they will not succeed,” he said.
“The President has only two options: either resign from office or pardon Gnanasara Thera,” Kassapa Thera declared.
“We are sending a red warning signal to the government. In the coming days, we will bring a large gathering of Buddhist monks to Colombo. Before that happens, we urge the government to take a step back and grant Gnanasara Thera an unconditional pardon,” he said.
“If that does not happen, the President will end up losing his presidency,” Kassapa Thera warned.
The protest demanding Gnanasara Thera’s release initially reached the Presidential Secretariat on October 15 following a march from Kandy.
However, after a court order restricted the protesters from remaining near the Presidential Secretariat, the monks relocated to Viharamahadevi Park on October 16.
The protesters have continued their satyagraha, including during heavy rainfall, insisting that they will remain at the location until their demand for Gnanasara Thera’s release is addressed.
Gnanasara Thera is serving a prison sentence following a conviction for contempt of court.
The protesting monks are demanding a presidential pardon for his release.

articles.title: Government intervention sought to revive Sri Lanka’s cinema industry
articles.text:
A group of representatives from Sri Lanka’s film industry has submitted a series of proposals aimed at addressing challenges facing the local cinema sector to Minister Sunil Handunnetti.
The proposals, prepared by the Independent Collective of Sri Lankan Cinema Professionals, were officially handed over to the Minister at Parliament on October 21.
According to Minister Handunnetti, the meeting brought together representatives of leading professional associations and institutions in the cinema industry to discuss measures needed to overcome existing challenges.
The Minister said he emphasised the need for government intervention to implement the proposals, safeguard the rights of artists and revitalise the local film industry.
Among those present were State Cinema Subcommittee Chairman and veteran filmmaker Anuruddha Jayasinghe, Sri Lanka Film Producers Association President Renuka Balasooriya, Art Directors Association President Bimal Dushmantha and Professional Makeup Artists Association President Nayana Ujith.
Representatives of film assistant directors, production managers and foreign film producers also attended the discussion.
The Minister did not provide details of the specific proposals or a timeline for their implementation.

articles.title: Prison population falls from nearly 42,000 to 37,000 in three months
articles.text:
The government has taken measures to expedite the issuance of Government Analyst’s reports to address delays that have contributed to prison overcrowding, Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara said.
Addressing Parliament today (22), the Minister revealed that 1,506 Government Analysts’ reports had been issued during August and September alone, following measures to strengthen the department’s workforce and fill existing vacancies.
He explained that delays in obtaining Government Analyst’s reports had been identified as one of the main factors contributing to overcrowding in prisons.
The Minister further stated that under proposed legislative amendments, the Government Analyst will be required to issue the relevant report within two months of receiving an item for examination.
Meanwhile, Minister Nanayakkara revealed that the number of prison inmates had decreased significantly following measures introduced to address overcrowding.
According to the Minister, the prison population had declined from 41,993 on July 1 to 36,925 by September 30, marking a reduction of 5,068 inmates.
He also outlined proposed legal amendments concerning the handling of narcotics seized as evidence in criminal cases.
Under the proposed changes, instead of retaining entire packages of narcotics until the conclusion of court proceedings, authorities will be permitted to photograph and, where necessary, video-record the substances before informing the relevant Magistrate.
The Magistrate will then be empowered to authorise the prompt destruction of the narcotics, subject to conditions imposed by the court.
Minister Nanayakkara emphasised that the proposed amendments are intended to ensure that these procedures are carried out lawfully, without affecting the fundamental rights of suspects or accused persons, including their right to a fair trial.

According to the Minister, the prison population had declined from 41,993 on July 1 to 36,925 by September 30, marking a reduction of 5,068 inmates.
