articles.title: New vehicle fitness test every 3 months or 5,000 km? DMT reveals plans
articles.text:
The Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) is planning to introduce mandatory roadworthiness tests for vehicles in Sri Lanka from early 2027, in addition to the existing vehicle emission tests.
Commissioner General of Motor Traffic, retired Air Marshal Thushara Fernando, said the proposed system is currently under discussion and has been referred to the department’s legal division.
Addressing a media briefing today (22), Fernando said the initiative is being developed under the guidance of the Transport Minister to improve vehicle safety.
Under the proposal, vehicle owners would be required to obtain a roadworthiness certificate from an authorized garage, in addition to the existing emission test certificate.
The department is considering requiring vehicle inspections at intervals of approximately 5,000 kilometers or three months.
Fernando said applications have been called from garages interested in conducting the inspections. Suitable garages will be selected based on criteria established by the department.
However, the Commissioner General did not clarify whether the proposed requirement would apply to all vehicles or only specific categories, such as passenger transport and commercial vehicles.
He also referred to the recent fatal road accident in Akurana, where a cement-carrying heavy vehicle reportedly suffered brake failure while travelling downhill, crashing into several other vehicles.
The Commissioner General said the proposed roadworthiness testing system remains at the discussion and legal review stage, with implementation targeted for early 2027.
The final scope, inspection requirements and implementation procedures have yet to be announced.
articles.summary: The Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) is planning to introduce mandatory roadworthiness tests for vehicles in Sri Lanka from early 2027, in addition to the existing vehicle emission tests. Under the proposal, vehicle owners would be required to obtain a roadworthiness certificate from an authorized garage, in addition to the existing emission test certificate.

articles.title: Small engine, big trouble? DMT clarifies motorcycle registration rules
articles.text:
The Department of Motor Traffic (DMT) has emphasised that registration is mandatory for motorcycles with engine capacities of 48cc or below 50cc, warning that legal action could be taken against those operating unregistered motorcycles on public roads.
Addressing a press conference today (22), Commissioner General of Motor Traffic, retired Air Marshal Thushara Fernando, clarified that motorcycles in this category must be registered despite claims suggesting otherwise.
He pointed out that certain motorcycle dealers have been informing customers that motorcycles with engine capacities below 50cc do not require registration.
The Commissioner General urged consumers to be cautious when purchasing such motorcycles and to ensure that they are provided with the necessary customs documentation.
He further warned that individuals found riding unregistered motorcycles on public roads could face legal action by the Police, including the imposition of fines.

articles.title: SriLankan Airlines extends suspension of Riyadh and Dammam flights until Nov 1
articles.text:
SriLankan Airlines has announced a further extension of the suspension of its flights between Colombo and the Saudi Arabian cities of Riyadh and Dammam until November 1, 2026, due to the prevailing security situation in the region.
In a statement issued today (22), the national carrier confirmed that all flights operating between Colombo and Riyadh, as well as Colombo and Dammam, will remain suspended up to and including November 1.
The airline stated that the decision was taken in consideration of the prevailing regional security situation, emphasising that the safety and security of passengers and crew remain its highest priority.
SriLankan Airlines further stated that flight services to the two destinations will resume once conditions have been assessed as suitable for commercial operations.
Passengers seeking further information have been advised to contact the airline through its hotline 1979 (within Sri Lanka), +94 11 777 1979 (international), or WhatsApp +94 74 444 1979 (chat only).
Further information is also available through travel agents or the airline’s official website, www.srilankan.com .
SriLankan Airlines thanked passengers for their understanding and cooperation during the suspension.
articles.summary: SriLankan Airlines has announced a further extension of the suspension of its flights between Colombo and the Saudi Arabian cities of Riyadh and Dammam until November 1, 2026, due to the prevailing security situation in the region.

articles.title: Over 30,000 identified in landslide high-risk areas: NBRI
articles.text:
More than 30,000 people living in high-risk areas have been identified and notified of potential landslide threats, while residents in medium-risk areas have also been alerted, a senior scientist at the National Building Research Institute (NBRI) said.
Wasantha Senadheera, senior geologist at the NBRI, warned that heavy rainfall following Cyclone Ditwah had increased the risk of landslides in several areas.
He said signs of potential landslides had been observed in several locations, while rocks and soil loosened or displaced during the Ditwah disaster could become unstable and slide due to the current heavy rainfall.
Senadheera urged residents, particularly those living in landslide-prone areas, to remain alert to their surroundings regardless of whether the Department of Meteorology or the NBRI had issued warnings.
He advised the public to follow safety instructions and pay attention to warning signs, including unusual sounds, prolonged heavy rainfall and cracks in the ground or structures.
Landslide alerts have been issued for several areas in Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Ratnapura, Badulla and Kegalle districts following heavy rainfall.
Senadheera made these remarks during a special government media briefing on the prevailing weather conditions.
Meanwhile, Department of Meteorology Forecasting Division Director Merril Mendis said a low-pressure area that had developed near Sri Lanka was located northwest of the island and was most likely to move westward.
The system was expected to bring heavy rainfall exceeding 100 millimeters to the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, North Western and Northern provinces, as well as the Galle and Matara districts, he said.
The effects of the low-pressure area were expected to continue in these regions throughout the following day, while rainy conditions were likely to persist for several more days.
Mendis attributed the continuing unsettled weather to the Intertropical Convergence Zone, a belt of low pressure near the equator where the northeast and southeast trade winds converge. The zone can contribute to the development of weather systems, including low-pressure areas.
Another low-pressure system is likely to develop near the Andaman Islands by Oct. 23, he said.
Although the system was not expected to have a direct impact on Sri Lanka, rainfall could continue until about Oct. 27 as winds move across the island, Mendis said.
Naval personnel and fishing communities have been warned to exercise caution when venturing to sea over the next few days, particularly in the Bay of Bengal, he added.

Wasantha Senadheera, senior geologist at the NBRI, warned that heavy rainfall following Cyclone Ditwah had increased the risk of landslides in several areas.
